subject: Urgent: sudden token-rate degradation after quant-profile rollout (customer escalation)
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: FastRetail Engineering Team <eng@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 22:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Hannah —

We started seeing a regression on Hosted API around 19:40 UTC. Our dashboards show p95 jumping from ~140ms to ~640ms and p99 hitting ~1.8s. More concerning: token-per-second (tokens/sec processed per request worker) dropped from ~220 TPS to ~45 TPS for the same model families. This started immediately after what we believe was your "quant-profile" rollout on the 19:30 maintenance window (we were notified of a non-disruptive update).

Attached a small perf snapshot (perf_snapshot_20261209.json) and a link to a trace (hosted_trace_link.txt). We also see increased 5xx counts on some requests (intermittent). This is impacting our checkout flows (real-time personalization).

Can someone confirm whether a kernel/quantization change rolled during that window? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is customer-critical for us.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Director, Platform Engineering
FastRetail

--
Attachment: perf_snapshot_20261209.json (json/summary)
Attachment: hosted_trace_link.txt (text/link)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
Cc: mar cus_lin@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 22:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Samantha — thank you for the report and for the attachments. I'm escalating this immediately. I've looped in Marcus (runtime), Grace (CS lead) and our on-call infra team.

Quick notes:
- We saw a scheduled rollout of an updated quantization profile to hosted nodes at ~19:25 UTC as part of a performance optimization. It was intended to prefer lower-precision kernels on eligible shapes.
- We are treating this as a high-priority escalation.

Next steps from our side: Marcus is running an analysis and will coordinate a rollback if we confirm correlation. Grace will follow up on customer impact and credit request. I'll keep you updated on the mitigation ETA within 30 minutes.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Phone: +1-415-555-0134

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 23:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Samantha / Hannah — I'm Marcus (runtime lead). I'm looking at the perf snapshot now. Preliminary findings:

- At 19:25 UTC we deployed quant-profile v1.2 to a subset of hosted instances (canary->gradual). That profile increases preference for int8 kernels on LLM attention/ffn paths for sequences <= 1024 tokens.
- On the samples in your snapshot, the runtime chose a different kernel path than before (kernel selector favored a newer vectorized int8 path). We see that for certain input shape distributions the int8 kernel exhibits lower single-token throughput due to memory layout / AVX interaction on the current instance type — this increases per-token latency and reduces tokens/sec for these requests.
- Batching behavior also changed: the new kernel increases per-request CPU/GPU stalls for heterogeneous sequence lengths, amplifying p95/p99.

Immediate asks: can you attach a representative prompt (payload) and a short trace of a slow request (the hosted_trace_link seems to contain a couple of traces but I need a full request body to reproduce CPU/GPU shape). If you can include the sequence length distribution for your workload that will help.

Mitigation plan (in order):
1) Pause the quant-profile rollout to affected hosts and revert to prior kernel selection for the canary pool.
2) If revert reduces impact, schedule a targeted kernel patch (optimize int8 layout) and re-run microbenchmarks with FastRetail sample inputs.
3) Provide a customer-facing postmortem and offer credit for business impact.

I'll attempt a canary rollback now and will post logs. ETA for initial revert: 1-2 hours.

Marcus Lin
Lead, Inference Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: FastRetail Engineering Team <eng@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 00:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Thanks Marcus — attaching a minimal repro and a sample production prompt (sample_prompt.txt). The heavy requests are mostly ~900-1100 tokens (avg ~980) with mixed shorter requests interleaved. The trace shows the slow request taking ~1.6s at the token emission stage, which matches your observation about per-token stalls.

We really need the canary rolled back if that will help. I'm also copying procurement (J. Kaur) since they'll need the credit paperwork if this extends.

Samantha

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 02:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Team — I've kicked off the automated rollback for the canary pool and started a hotfix branch to address the kernel layout issue. Current status:

- Canary rollback to quant-profile v1.1 initiated at 02:05 UTC; progress: 60% of canary hosts reverted.
- Early metrics from reverted hosts show tokens/sec returning to ~200-230 TPS and p95 dropping back toward baseline for test traffic.
- We're keeping the rollout paused. We'll run A/B microbenchmarks with FastRetail sample payloads before reintroducing any change.

Expect a full canary rollback within ~90 minutes from now (~03:40 UTC). I'll post the rollback logs and a link to the infra trace in INF-4821.

Dylan Brooks
On-call Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, Samantha Ortiz <samantha@fastretail.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: API latency spike and throughput drop - urgent

Samantha / Hannah — thanks for working through this with us. Quick summary and next steps for FastRetail: 

- Root cause (preliminary): quant-profile v1.2 resulted in different kernel selection on a subset of hosted nodes which, for FastRetail's input shape distribution (~900-1100 tokens with variability), reduced token-per-second throughput and raised p95/p99 due to batching/shape interaction.
- Mitigation: Canary rollback completed; affected hosts reverted to quant-profile v1.1. We validated with FastRetail sample payloads — tokens/sec and p95/p99 have largely returned to expected ranges.
- Next: Marcus & Dylan will produce a technical postmortem (INF-4821) with timeline, fix plan, and test coverage. We'll schedule a joint runbook review with FastRetail engineers to avoid similar surprises when we optimize quant kernels.

Customer impact handling: Hannah will coordinate a service credit for the disruption; we'll aim to have a credit offer and a scheduled postmortem call within 48 hours.

Grace O'Connor
Head, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
